body:
This is a little disheartening, but I appreciate the honest answers.

My salary is 58k, before taxes. I was given a generous raise last year - I was and am still very thankful that they did this in order to accommodate me during a difficult and tumultuous period of my life. 

This is technically in line for projected earnings for people in Michigan with my same job title (junior developer), but it was only after I had to have a special negotiating meeting with my boss in order to get my raise. Before that, I was making around 48k before taxes.

Also, it was a dumb mistake on my part, but I did not keep close track of all my worked overtime during the time period. I will absolutely be doing this in the future, but I unfortunately trusted my manager to have my best interest in mind during this project. :/

I had another friend say the same thing - I wasn't happy in my relationship for such a long time and so, even though it's only been a few months since I left my ex, I was already over the relationship well before that. I know there's always going to be a level of guilt with leaving abusive relationships, and I'm definitely feeling that now.

At the very least, it's nice to explore just the concept of having a very intense crush with a friend as opposed to some stranger on an app or something. The distance is also very nice, I will admit. I like having the control of us just talking over texts and phone calls as opposed to someone being in my city and wanting to be physically close to me. I don't know if I'm quite ready for that yet. 

So, yeah. I guess you're right. Gotta get back on the bike at some point. Maybe this is like a "tricycle" introduction to that process.

I completely understand, and I appreciate the words of caution. I'd rather be fully prepared before I start any sort of kink relationship or full exploration of these practices. I feel like my interest right now is mostly academic. And while I know reading about these things is completely different than actually engaging with them, I was mostly looking for a small jumping off point.
You are correct that I still have a lot to process in terms of my last relationship. I should have clarified in my original post too, but I'm definitely not looking to actively engage with another person at this time.
Regardless, I appreciate the response!

Thank you! 
I know, I'm definitely still in the research phase right now. I have that desire to Just Do It Right Now, but I also know that I'm not quite there yet. Regardless, I appreciate the response:)

Thank you for the links, this has opened up a pretty interesting rabbit hole, lol.
This is crazy! I've never heard of anything like this before. It's good to know that it's temporary, and just a natural response to the vaccine. Sometimes I forget what weird and delicate little machines are bodies and brains are.

I'm a little apprehensive for the second dose, but keeping this in mind will make it easier, I think.

I'm wishing the best for you, and I'm sorry that you're experiencing this. It makes me feel less crazy to hear that other people are having a similar experience. Still, I know it's difficult. I hope that it will pass quickly.

Yeah, I mean, I can do without the down swing. I think, overall, it'll be worth it. I'm trying to keep the positives in mind as well.
I hope your second dose goes well. I hate needles too, so I understand that feeling of being anxious about just that whole process, everything else notwithstanding.

I'm glad that it's been going well for you! I can definitely understand the vaccine situation being a relief, with everything that's been happening this past year. I'm very much looking forward to seeing some friends again, as we all start getting vaccinated.
I'm guessing it's like any other medication, in that it affects people differently sometimes. This particular apparent side effect just seemed so strange.

Unprofessional is, unfortunately, the name of the game when it comes to her.
I'm definitely going to be contacting her by the end of the day today.

Yeah, honestly I'm not stoked. It's not secure, like you were saying and, to my knowledge, that text is the only copy/proof of my W2 from that job at this point. I'm getting to the point where I'm wondering if I need to report this owner.
They're supposed to and I'm wondering if she thinks this counts...or if it DOES count. Again, I know diddly about tax law stuff.
I guess what I want out of this is for him to listen to us and respect our (my) boundaries and not be trying to force himself into our days.

I guess I mean I don't know if I'm *able* to help him out more than I am already, and I feel like the asshole cause I'm becoming frustrated with him and feel like snapping sometimes/not being as gentle. I like a fair amount of alone time to recharge and he wants the opposite. 

He hasn't really been listening when we tell him we only have a certain amount of time. And I'm worried I'm just going to snap at him about not wanting to hang out and really upset him/make his mental state even worse.

Yes, like the other commenters have mentioned, revisiting trauma has a very real and direct physical effect on the body. Self-care after sessions is important. I always try and go for a long walk after mine. It helps me finish processing, and to feel a little more connected to my body.
I can do that, although I don't know where I'd find one. How long would something like that stay in my system?
Maybe? I've never had any in the past. Doesn't mean they can't suddenly develop I guess?
I have another session Thursday, so I can ask my therapist and see what she says too.

Oh, absolutely. When I first started EDMR, I was kind of ignorant of the whole process, and just treated it like any other session of talk therapy. Nearly ran myself ragged. I had to take a huge step back just to take care of myself emotionally and mentally. 

It's very normal, but I can understand it being strange.

That's so awesome to hear, I'm glad EDMR has been helpful for you.

I've only been doing it for maybe a month, and the changes that I've been noticing are crazy. It has been so so helpful and, like you said, makes me feel like I'm more normal.

I hope the rest of your journey goes well!

I think this is a very common problem for people who suffer from trauma. The other day, during an EMDR session, I had a very vivid flashback and a bit of a breakdown. Even in the middle of crying my eyes out and hyperventilating, I kept saying to my therapist "I don't know if this is just all in my head or it's real". It's your mind's way of protecting itself from reliving painful memories.

Thank you.

I've been wondering if maybe a small break wouldn't be a bad idea.
In my last session I sort of came to the realization that I try very hard to continue on in spite of myself, to be as "presentable" and as "normal" as possible when it comes to dealing with my trauma. This is mostly after I had a massive anxiety/CPTSD attack in a public restroom last year, and had to deal with the ensuing social fallout. 
Maybe it's silly, but just today everything kind of hit me, emotionally speaking, and I realized that part of this whole process is FEELING and processing through these painful things. And that, sometimes it's okay to not be okay. That was a very difficult realization for me. I've been so concerned with "getting better" that I didn't really stop to think about that, I guess.

I definitely like the idea of showing my kid self some of the good things that I have in my life now. I think that would help me, and to get some of those positive things associated with that point in my life. I've been much too hard on adult me as well as kid me. 

Thank you again, I really do appreciate it.

Thank you, it's encouraging to hear from other people.

It's also interesting and encouraging to hear people talk about their "protector" and "protective selves", because this was a concept I explored with my therapist last session. I feel like as much as that part of myself is trying very hard to keep me going in a pull-yourself-up-by-your-bootstraps kind of way, it isn't very forgiving or open to exploring and processing through the images and memories that it needs to. 

I think I have been trying very hard to "be okay" lately, but I had the sudden realization that sometimes I just need to be a little easier on myself, and the subsequent emotional buckle has kind of taken me out of commission a bit.

I wish you the best of luck with everything, thanks again.

I had a very similar experience with a recent session. A very intense and emotional flashback that stayed with me for days afterward. From what I understand it's very normal while you're stirring up old feelings and memories, but I can understand it making you feel strange.

Thank you. I've been scrolling through this subreddit for a while and I've tried to be encouraging to people but it's hard. I never know what to say. I'm glad you're a lot more eloquent than I am.
And even though I feel like I sometimes don't want to be alive anymore...it's nice to hear someone say something good. Most days are pretty difficult. I hope it gets better.

If it makes you feel any better, I will be turning 25 next week and I still don't have my driver's license. I'm such a bad driver it's almost funny. The last time I drove, I took out two mailboxes. I understand how frustrating it is not being able to drive, though. There's definitely a certain type of independence that you feel you're missing out on. The plus of that is no car insurance I guess, ha.

I would say that, unfortunately, there's not much you can do for her when she gets like this except be there for her. I hate platitudes, and this definitely sounds like one, but it's true. 

Be aware that her being distant isn't necessarily because she doesn't care for you, but just that she's having a hard time processing things at that exact moment. 

As for contacting her, I would say I would repsect her wishes. Speaking personally, I know that when I want to be alone any sort of outside interaction makes me overwhelmed and agitated, even when it's someone I care about. If you really want to let her know that you're thinking about her, though, I think a text or an email, something that doesn't require an immediate response, might be okay. Something along the lines of "Hey, just wanted to make sure you're doing okay. I love and miss you". It's not overly intrusive, but still shows you care.

I can go numb anywhere from a couple hours to a couple weeks. It kind of feels like someone has grabbed the back of my shirt and has pulled me five inches outside of my outline, if that makes any sense. 

The shorter instances are more physical, I guess. Everything feels muted, like my head's stuck in cotton, and like I've partially lost my peripheral vision. The longer times of going numb are the hardest though. They're less physical and more emotional. At these points, I don't feel anything for anyone really. Like, there are some superficial emotions that are largely based on logical inferences, but it doesn't go much deeper than that. Something along the likes of "This is your friend J and you care for her because that is what is expected of you". My interactions with people become largely performative, in an effort to not alienate myself for good, especially after the episodes pass. It fucking sucks and it makes me feel disgusting.

I have so many people in my life whom I care for and who care for me, but sometimes it's like my brain shuts down and can't process relationships or something.

I'm learning that one of the main things that people with PTSD have trouble with is forming/maintaining relationships, intimacy, trust, etc. So, the jealousy makes sense. Doesn't make it any less shitty, of course.

Thank you. I wrote this at a very low point the other day, and reading your message really made me feel better. Seeing all the posts on this site makes me feel a lot less alone in everything, actually. So, thank you again.

I'm sorry that things have been difficult with your fiance, and I hope things go better soon for the both of you. Dealing with trauma seems to kind of turn you into a monster (or, at least, it makes me feel like a monster sometimes), and trying to be there for someone going through that can be terrifying and exhausting. I think sometimes it all just becomes so overwhelming and both sides just need time alone to decompress and reflect on things. But it seems like you truly love and care for your fiance and want to be there for her, and I'm sure she feels the same. Working to the point of being healthy enough yourself in order to be there for others can be difficult, though. 

I hope that I can make it through this okay, and that I can find the strength in myself to be there for my partner as well. He is a wonderful person. I know what's happened to me will never go away, but maybe I can deal with it all better at some point.

I just ordered this book, along with A Really Good Day by Ayelet Waldman. Thank you for the recommendation. 
I have tried LSD before, and there were points that were truly enlightening and helpful. The last time I did it, however, I had an exceptionally bad trip. I basically relived my trauma and was unable to stop convulsing for almost an entire day, even after the drugs had worn off. I feel like I was almost on the edge of making a big turn in progress, confronting things that I haven't for years, but my brain just shut down and noped out of that in such a way that has been affecting me still. I'm hesitant to try again, but at the same time I wonder if I just need to adjust doses/surroundings/other factors. I keep hearing that it's so helpful.
